title: Deciding the size of the move becomes part of the run
description:
## As asked

Repository: JKershaw/LinearViewer (Harbour).

**What this is for.** Before work starts, Harbour can look at a ticket from two angles: the task up close, and the code around it (the two Survey stages). Today a person starts both by hand. Their notes reach the work only through a "How to go about it" section that the person also writes by hand. That hand-written scope is where this week's mistakes came from. One wording invited a copy. A sweep was drawn around a list of names instead of the behaviour. A description in the scope was turned by the builder into a comment that wasn't true. All three were hand-offs that said too much about how (on main: `docs/papers/harbour/cleaner-than-it-started.md`, Finding 9).

**What we want.** Harbour carries this. Before work starts, it runs the look-first step. A following step then reads both notes and lays out the sizes of move on offer, from just doing the task up to a larger move in the area, or saying this is the wrong work, and recommends one. The area's notes and the latest Periodical readings should feed it too. Those arrive in later tickets of this round, so read them where they exist and work without them where they don't.

How big the move is stays a person's call. They can answer it as a ruling, or set a standing policy in advance so the run goes ahead without stopping. John's standing answer is "err larger". Either way, the chosen size is written on the ticket in plain words: what we're doing and why, not how. The builder works out the how.

Two things we learned about larger moves. Do the big ones early rather than after the small ones, so the small ones land on the new shape. And when a ticket takes on something beyond its own task, make that extra its own piece of work, which may stop and say so if it turns out not to pay.

Since 2 November we have treated the look-first step as advice, not a gate, with no review loop of its own (on main: `docs/plans/survey.md`). Keep it that way.

**Appetite:** err larger.

**Done looks like:** a ticket John files goes from filed to building with no one writing its scope by hand, and the size it chose, and why, reads plainly on the ticket. A small, clear ticket stays small.

*End of what was asked. Steps write below this line; nothing above it changes.*

## Implementation Plan

*Implemented and closed 8 Nov 2026.* The plan (revision 1, approved 7 Nov 22:42) and its builder notes are in the task snapshots and the comment trail. This stub replaces them.

## Outcome

Implemented in four pieces, as the approved plan described, plus two later corrections:

* **Piece 1, LIN-4367 (PR #2354):** the code PR #2351 left behind was simplified.
* **Piece 2, LIN-4368 (PR #2355):** the size record, its guard and the policy.
* **Piece 3, LIN-4369 (PR #2356):** scoping sizes the move, proven by replay.
* **Piece 4, LIN-4370 (PR #2370):** code runs the look-first sequence at both recommendation seams.
* **LIN-4393 (PR #2377):** removed the size setting John rejected. err-larger is now built in.
* **PR [https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2380:](<https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2380:>)** scoping's area-notes pointer. Merged as `6ebadd305` and deployed 8 Nov 16:44 UTC.

How the work moved from the plan:

* **The record.** It became four lines (Size, Why, Cuts, Decided by), and scoping posts no comment. This was John's ruling `lin4346-size-after-arm2` (arm 4).
* **The weighing.** The options weighed and any note citations go only in scoping's final message.
* **The policy.** It is built in rather than a workspace setting (LIN-4393).

The hands-off witness has not run yet; see the close-out comment. It needs a fresh ticket John files, which autopilot then takes through the Surveys and scoping with **Decided by:** the standing policy. Scoping's final message should name the area note it weighed. If it fails, the next step is `bug` on this task.

This work needs multiple sessions (pieces 1 → 4, as subtasks).

**Before you start (John's ruling on LIN-4345, 7 Nov 18:03): naming each cut to the ask belongs here.**

LIN-4345 replayed review twelve times against two tickets where an ask had been narrowed (`docs/reviews/lin-4345-per-sentence-replay-2026-11-07.md`). Review caught the narrowing every time it had been named ("Out of scope — split out"), and missed it every time it hadn't, however review was worded. On 1 November, "a full guide" became "sequence the human's few clicks" at scoping and was never called a cut, so review approved a thin guide.

John chose to move the next attempt upstream. Whatever decides how big the move is, and what's in or out of it, names each cut to what the person asked, in plain words, and sends it to a ruling unless the person already agreed. That's scoping and plan today, and the size step this ticket builds. Then review only has to check that a cut was agreed. It doesn't have to spot one that was never named.

This is part of the same move as the size step, not a separate gate. Choosing a size is where a cut to the ask gets made.

**Done also means** that if the 1 November request were run again, the cut from "a full guide" would come to a person as a ruling before anything was built.

**Update (7 Nov, 22:15 UTC):** LIN-4345's second attempt has merged ([PR #2351](https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2351), `11dc1d7bd`). Scoping and plan now name each cut to the ask and raise one ruling. Its replay: 3/3 named the cut at scoping against 0/3 before, and review flagged a named cut 3/3. So the note above is partly done already. The size step should carry that rule, not build a second one. A size of move that cuts the ask is a named cut like any other. The guide's size cap is now a separate follow-up on the prompt-size budget's reach (John's ruling on LIN-4345).

## Survey open-0: LIN-4346 @ 11dc1d7bd

**Why it will be difficult**

1. **"Advice, not a gate" is built today as "cannot run".** Both Surveys have `route: null` (`lib/prompt-template-defs.js:1198,1225`). The router throws "cannot be recommended", and `tests/unit/lin-4248-survey-stages.test.js` pins all of this. Running the Survey means breaking those pins while keeping what they protect: nothing routes on the Survey's verdict, and it has no review loop. That invariant needs restating, not deleting.

2. **There is no seam for "before the first stage".** The run's order lives in the autopilot kickoff prompt, about 60 KB of prose (`lib/prompts/autopilot-kickoff.js`) under the byte freeze. Adding "survey, then decide" there is the cheap path, and it is what the plan warns about: "gates are where prose collects."

3. **The deciding step replaces the operator's hand, and that hand's best rules were "how".** The log's scope rules are method: delete copies in the same change or name the guard, big moves early, the extra as its own piece with a stop rule (`docs/plans/survey/log.md` ~2008–2317). Yet two of the four copies the after-steps gathered came from the operator's own scope constraints (~2182). So the ticket aims at a symptom. The trouble was never that a person wrote the scope. The scope carried how. A step that writes it automatically repeats the mistake faster unless the format itself leaves no room for how.

4. **It lands on LIN-4345, merged at this base.** Under the CUT rule (`lib/prompts/stage-intent.js:8`), any `## As asked` clause not delivered in full needs a `DECISION:` ruling. A "smaller" or "wrong work" size has to be that same ruling, not a second one. A "larger" size makes its extra a separate piece, but workers can't enqueue, and the notebook says to file tickets only when John asks.

5. **A standing policy has nowhere to live.** The ruling code (`unanswered-decisions.js`, `task-decisions-store.js`) counts unanswered rulings and has nothing that answers one in advance. The smallest home is a workspace preference that answers the size ruling and records that it did, not a new policy store.

6. **"Small stays small" pulls against "err larger".** A step that always lays out sizes, under a standing "larger", will find something on every ticket (the June misfire, LIN-391) unless "the task only" is easy for it to say.

Area notes don't exist in code. Periodicals can be read at `/periodicals/{id}`.

**What I'd do first**

Fix the output before the wiring: a short fixed block below `## As asked` giving the size, the options weighed and why, with no files and no steps. Then run a pre-registered replay, as LIN-4345 did, on LIN-4178 (wording that invited a copy), LIN-4252 and LIN-4253 (copies left and not left), and a small clear control such as LIN-998. Wire it in only if the control stays small and the how stays out. By "big moves early", this ticket should also take the routing seam and the restated invariant, so the round's later tickets build on the new shape.

## Survey global: LIN-4346 @ 11dc1d7bd

**Where it lands.** The stage templates (`lib/prompt-template-defs.js`, 1,256 lines; both Surveys `route: null`), the selector and its code-settled route (`lib/stage-router.js`, `lib/recommendation-facts.js`), and the ruling path (`DECISION:` → `task-decisions-store` / `unanswered-decisions`). The area is improving. A stage's traits are declared once (LIN-4253), and the cut rule has one home in `STAGE_INTENT`'s DECIDE (LIN-4345). But a kind is still named by hand in about ten tables, and census tests cover most of them. `wall-clock-summary`'s `bucketOf` has no test, and a kind missing from it is silently counted as orchestration (LIN-1653 was that bug).

**The obvious way would add:**
- **A `size` template beside `scoping`.** That gives two stages that settle what gets delivered. Scoping already writes In/Out of Scope and, since LIN-4345, keeps each cut with its ruling. A second home for cut rulings is the duplicate the brief rules out.
- **Surveys that run on their own.** The selector can't pick them (`route: null`), so the easy route is a code fact ("no Survey at this base → survey first"). But CLAUDE.md says code settles *only* the review-loop bound, and nothing fails if that goes stale. Two Surveys plus sizing is three sessions before any work, which a small ticket pays unless code lets it skip.
- **A standing "err larger" policy.** Nothing like it exists; its home is `workspace-preferences.js`, next to `dispatchDefaults`. `settings-areas.js`'s census fails on a key with no area, so that one would be noticed. A one-off ruling needs no new card: `DECISION:` carries it, and selector rule 1 already respects it.
- **The written size.** It goes below the As-asked block via `description/below`. Close-out's prune step replaces scoping sections there, so prune has to keep the size line or the "why" is lost at merge.

**Better, and this task can carry it.** Make sizing *scoping's* job rather than a sibling's. Scoping reads both Survey comments when they exist, lays out drill / small tidy / consolidate / Theseus / wrong work, recommends one, and writes the what and why where it already writes scope. A smaller-than-asked size is already a cut under CUT's wording. Scoping's `route.when` then has to cover "not yet sized", which changes the byte-pinned selector fixtures. Name the Survey trigger in the invariant beside the review-loop bound, and put its skip in code. Any new kind goes in `bucketOf`, or the bucket is derived from the template.

**A deeper symptom.** The mistakes in Finding 9 came from a hand-off that said *how*. A size step that names files or helpers would repeat them in a model's voice. Pin "what and why, no how" with a test on the written section, not only with prompt prose.

**Not this task's to carry.** Derive every per-kind table from the template, as was done for `route` and `writes`. Also, `docs/plans/survey.md`'s "John is asked only when the large option is recommended" contradicts this ticket. Under the policy, larger goes ahead without asking and smaller-than-asked gets a ruling. The notebook should say so.

## Size of the move (the person's call)

Err larger, John's standing answer.

**What this ticket is really about.** The Surveys made it sharper. This week's mistakes didn't come from a person writing the scope. They came from scope that said how: wording that invited a copy, a sweep drawn around a list of names, a description that became a false comment. A step that writes scope automatically would repeat that faster, unless what it writes leaves no room for how. A separate size step would also be a second place deciding what gets delivered. Since LIN-4345 merged, scoping already does that: it names each cut to the person's ask and raises it as a ruling (the "cut rule").

**So sizing becomes part of scoping, and the look-first step becomes part of the run.** Before work starts, the two Surveys run. Scoping reads what they found, weighs the sizes on offer, recommends one, and writes the chosen size on the ticket as what and why only, with no files and no steps. Hold that line with something stronger than prompt wording. A size smaller than what was asked is a cut, so it goes through the cut rule's ruling, not a second one. When a ticket takes on something beyond its own task, that extra is its own piece of work, and it's allowed to stop and say so if it turns out not to pay. The Surveys stay advice: nothing routes on what they say, and they have no review loop.

**What John means by "err larger".** Lean towards the larger move when the look shows it pays, and when in doubt. It doesn't mean inflating every ticket. A clear, small ticket stays small, and "just the task" should be as easy to recommend as anything else. The standing policy is a setting a person makes once. The run reads it and says that it did.

**Spend.** Running both Surveys on every ticket adds sessions. That's accepted for now, because John's stance is that cost is measured, not optimised, while we learn whether the loop works. Record what it costs per ticket so it can be tuned later.

**Before wiring it in,** replay it on past tickets with the pass criterion written down first: one whose wording invited a copy (LIN-4178), a tidy that left copies and one that didn't (LIN-4252, LIN-4253), and a small, clear control. Have a fresh reader who didn't build it judge the result.

**Also finish what LIN-4345's last change left in this code.** PR #2351 was read blind twice, as mixed both times: passes BS and BT on LIN-4150. Its leftovers are in the code you'll be reworking. The biggest is the prompt-size budget test turning into a second change log.

**Questions:** settle engineering questions yourself, and record why. Raise a ruling only for John's calls: how big a move is, what's spent, and authority. He'll answer in the morning, and work that doesn't depend on a ruling keeps moving.

**Done when** running the loop takes nothing more than setting the policy once and filing a ticket. That ticket is looked at and sized with no one writing its scope by hand, the size reads plainly on it as what and why, a small clear ticket stays small, and the code around the cut rule is simpler than PR #2351 left it.

Plan written into the description (`## Implementation Plan`, at `11dc1d7bd`). Sizing becomes scoping's output: one guarded `## Size of the move` record. Code runs Surveys → scoping for a ticket with no size yet. The `sizePolicy` workspace preference (`ask` / `err-larger`) answers the size ruling. Four pieces in order: (1) simplify the code PR #2351 left, (2) the size record, its guard and the policy, (3) scoping sizes, replayed before wiring on LIN-4178/4252/4253 with LIN-998 as the control, (4) the code route and the restated invariant. No cuts to the As-asked block; my three readings are listed for plan-review. Needs breakdown after plan-review.

### Plan Review Verdict

**Verdict:** Request Changes. The approach is sound, but the code route as specified would skip John's usual tickets and can re-send scoping in a loop.

Blocking findings: 2

**How it meets what was asked.** "A ticket John files goes from filed to building with no one writing its scope by hand, and the size it chose, and why, reads plainly on the ticket. A small, clear ticket stays small." The plan meets this through piece 4's code route plus pieces 2 and 3. It makes no cuts. I accept the three readings (see below). Finding 1 is a place where the plan, built as written, would narrow this without anyone choosing to.

Checked at `11dc1d7bd`. That is still `origin/main`: nothing has landed since the plan was written, so the files it touches are unchanged. These anchors hold: `loopBoundRecommendation` / `getRecommendation`, `rejectExcludedKind` (`lib/action-kind.js:17`), `refusedByAsAsked` and its two call sites (`routes/proxy-writes.js:478,566`), the close-out prune (`lib/prompt-template-defs.js:1063`), the Survey templates and their headings, `prepareRecommendationInput`, the pinned-kind `generatePrompt` in `lib/dispatch-entrance.js`, `loadRecentRuns` (runs carry `kind`), `GET /issues/:id/cost`, CLAUDE.md at 110 lines with the invariant at :102, and `docs/plans/survey.md:96`. `GET /periodicals` returns run state, and `/periodicals/:id` is a POST mint. The plan's reading of "no readings yet" is right, and the open Survey's `/periodicals/{id}` claim is wrong.

---

#### Blocking 1. "No person's comment waiting" turns the route off for the tickets John actually files

Piece 4 says the route applies only when "no person's comment is waiting to be acted on… read the same way the selector's facts read 'acted after'". In code that reading is `assembleTrailFacts().latestPerson.actedAfter` (`lib/recommendation-facts.js:566-571`). Two things make it true:

- `isPersonComment` counts any comment that doesn't open with a heading. That includes John's "**Before you start…**" and "**For when you start…**" notes.
- `actedAfter` is true only after an agent note (`autopilot…`, `plan posted…`), landed work or a close-out. Survey comments and a scoping record do not count.

So a ticket filed with a context comment never enters the sequence. Rule 1 doesn't name a stage, and the selector can't offer the Surveys (`route: null`), so it moves on to plan. Once a plan exists, the route is off for good. The ticket reaches building with no size on it. That is not an edge case: the next two tickets in this round, LIN-4347 and LIN-4350, each carry exactly such a comment, as LIN-4346 did. Also, in production the selector gets `runs`, and the comment-derived "acted after" line is left out (`formatTrailFactsBlock`, and `docs/architecture/prompt-system.md:7`). So "the same way the selector's facts read it" has no single meaning to copy.

**What to change:** say what the exclusion is protecting (a person's word that holds the work or redirects it) and define it so filing context feeds the sequence instead of switching it off. The Surveys and scoping already read the trail, so the comments reach them. My recommendation: person's comments posted before the ticket's first run are part of the filing and never turn the route off. A person's comment after a run has started yields to rule 1 until a later run exists. Both can be computed from `runs`. Add a witness: a ticket with a "Before you start" comment and no runs gets `survey-task`.

#### Blocking 2. The route can re-send scoping without end, and the plan's own guard can cause it

Surveys get the "attempted" rule (a comment, or a run of that kind exists), so a failure never holds the work. Scoping doesn't get one. Its only exit is "no size section". Any scoping run that ends without a stored record sends scoping again on the next tick, past the selector and past `blocked`. The likeliest cause comes from this plan: piece 2's guard returns 422 for a record that quotes an As-asked clause containing a code span or path (LIN-4346's own block has one), or that numbers its options. Each scoping run then fails the same way, overnight, while John answers rulings in the morning. The eligibility list also leaves out what rule 3 would stop: an open blocker relation, or an unanswered ruling on the ticket.

**What to change:** give scoping the same attempted rule as the Surveys. Once a scoping run has ended since the Surveys and no record exists, fall through to the selector rather than re-sending. Add "no open blocker relation and no unanswered ruling" to the eligibility list. Add witnesses for both. The pending-ruling re-entry case keeps working, because it goes through scoping's `route.when`, not the code route.

---

#### Notes for the builder (not blocking)

1. **Two seams, not one.** The UI's streaming paths call `getRecommendationStream`, which runs its own `loopBoundRecommendation` (`lib/openrouter.js:1113`) and only falls back to `getRecommendation` behind a proxy. Recommend-and-dispatch and autopilot go through `computeRecommendation` (`routes/proxy.js`). Make the look-first step a sibling of `loopBoundRecommendation` (or generalise it into one code-route helper) called at both seams, and test both. Otherwise the task page would show a different next step than autopilot takes.
2. **The guard and quoted cuts.** The record must "quote each cut", and As-asked text can contain code spans and paths. Exempt text that matches the As-asked block word for word. Write the weighed sizes as bullets so the numbered-steps check doesn't trip. Add both to the two-sided guard tests.
3. **Heading collision and tickets in flight.** John's hand-written `## Size of the move (the person's call)` *comments* already exist on LIN-4346, LIN-4348 and LIN-4358. Make the parser read only the description section below the block, and decide on purpose what happens to tickets with Surveys and a hand size comment but no plan (LIN-4348, LIN-4358): after merge the route would send them to scoping. Either is defensible, but state which in the plan and give it a test.
4. **Replay mechanics.** The Survey prompts resolve `origin/main` themselves and embed `issue.description` "as they read now" (`formatSurveyTicketText`). A replay at each ticket's historical base therefore needs the ticket text as filed and the base pinned in the render. `scripts/survey-replay-*.mjs` and `steady-base-render*.mjs` already do this, so reuse them and don't write new ones.
5. **`acted after` in docs.** If finding 1 changes how the route reads a person's comment, restate it where the invariant is restated (CLAUDE.md:102, `prompt-system.md`, the stage-router comment) so the two code-settled routes and rule 1 are described consistently.
6. **Settings → Running** currently lists only `features` and `routes`. `sizePolicy` is a preference with its own POST route. Register the route in the area's `routes` so the census sees it, and show the policy in the area's `state`.

#### The three readings

- *The extra as its own piece inside the ticket* (first subtask or first commits, droppable with a reason, no new tickets). This fits the ask and the "workers gain no authority to file" constraint. Accepted.
- *Big moves early, within the ticket.* Accepted as the size step's job. When the larger move is one that sibling tickets should land on, the record can say so in what/why terms (for example, "LIN-4350 should land on this"). That passes it to whoever schedules without giving the worker scheduling authority.
- *Area notes and readings absent until LIN-4347/LIN-4349.* Correct at HEAD. See the Periodicals check above.

Everything else holds: piece 1 lands first so later ceiling raises land on the new shape, the shared record module, sizing as scoping's output, the replay gate before wiring, and keeping Surveys as advice (routing on whether they happened, never on what they said). Revise piece 4's eligibility and termination for findings 1 and 2, then return for a short re-review.

Plan revised (revision 1, answering the plan review of 22:33). The `## Implementation Plan` in the description has been replaced in place, still at `11dc1d7bd` (unchanged `origin/main`).

- **Blocking 1:** a person's comment holds the look-first route only if it was posted after the sequence started (the first run or first Survey comment, whichever came first) and nothing has run since. Filing notes like "Before you start" now feed the Surveys and scoping. Witness: a ticket with such a comment and no runs gets `survey-task`.
- **Blocking 2:** scoping is attempted at most once, like the Surveys (a record, or any scoping run on record). After that the route steps aside to the selector, so a failed or guard-refused scoping run can't loop. An open blocker, or a newest run waiting on a person, also turns the route off.
- **Notes:** one code-route helper serves both `getRecommendation` and `getRecommendationStream`. The guard exempts quotes that match the As-asked text word for word, and options are bullets. The parser reads only the description. LIN-4348 and LIN-4358 go to scoping once, which turns John's hand-written size comment into a guarded record decided by a ruling. The replay pins the base and the ticket text as filed, using the existing survey-replay and steady-base scripts. Settings → Running registers the policy route and shows its state.

No cuts to the As-asked block. Returning for the short re-review. `plan-review due: yes`.

### Plan Review Verdict

**Verdict:** Approve. Revision 1 fixes both blockers, and the four builder notes left below don't change the plan's shape.

**How it meets what was asked.** "A ticket John files goes from filed to building with no one writing its scope by hand, and the size it chose, and why, reads plainly on the ticket. A small, clear ticket stays small." Piece 4's code route, the size record from pieces 2–3, and the LIN-998 control replay meet this. There are no cuts. The three readings were accepted at 22:33 and still hold.

**What I checked.** I checked against `11dc1d7bd`, which is still `origin/main`. Nothing has landed since the plan was written, so every file it touches is unchanged. I read `lib/recent-runs.js`, `lib/recommendation-input.js`, `lib/recommendation-facts.js` (`isPersonComment`), `lib/dispatch-terminal.js` (how a run comes to read "waiting on a person"), `lib/unanswered-decisions.js`, `lib/prompts/stage-intent.js` (CUT), the Survey templates, and both seams in `lib/openrouter.js` (`:1113`, `:1972`, helper at `:1925`). I also looked at the run history of LIN-4348 and LIN-4358 through `/issues/{id}/cost`.

**The last verdict, point by point**
- **Blocking 1 (filing comments switched the route off): fixed, and the fix holds.** Comments posted before the sequence starts now count as part of the filing. The sequence starts at the earlier of the first run and the first Survey comment, and both can be computed from the comments and runs. The witness covers the shape LIN-4347 and LIN-4350 have. Survey comments open with a heading, so `isPersonComment` already never treats them as a person's comment (`lib/recommendation-facts.js:101`).
- **Blocking 2 (scoping could be re-sent forever): fixed.** Scoping is attempted once, the same way as the Surveys, so a failed or guard-refused scoping run falls through to the selector one time and stops there. An open blocker is now in the eligibility list. "No unanswered ruling" is covered only partly; see note 1. Termination doesn't depend on that check, because once all three steps have been attempted the route is closed.
- **Notes 1–6:** all answered in place: both seams use one helper, quotes matching As-asked are exempt from the guard and options are bullets, the parser reads only the description, the in-flight tickets are decided, the replay pins the base and the ticket text as filed, and Settings → Running registers the policy route and shows its state.

#### Notes for the builder (not blocking)

1. **An unanswered ruling stands the route aside only while its run is parked.** A run reads "waiting on a person" only while its last wake marker is `[blocked]` (`deriveBlockedStatus`, `lib/dispatch-terminal.js:269`). CUT's "`DECISION:` before `BLOCKED:`" does park the run, so a cut ruling raised that way is covered. A `DECISION:` raised on the way to completion, though, lands on a run that ended `done`. `lib/unanswered-decisions.js:10-13` says outright that a decision is separate from "waiting". So piece 4's sentence "an unanswered ruling stands the route aside" claims more than the code does. Scoping's own size ruling is safe anyway, because the pending record turns the route off. What's left is a ruling raised before sizing by an earlier stage that then ended: the route can still send the remaining look-first steps, at most once each, and those steps read the ruling on the trail. Either say exactly that in the plan and in the restated invariant, or read the ticket's open decisions (`openDecisionLoopIds`) if that's cheap from the recommendation path. Don't add a new store read just for this. Add a witness for whichever you choose: a run that ended `done` with an open `DECISION:`.
2. **The full run list isn't on the input yet.** `loadRecentRuns` already cuts the list to 5 inside the function (`lib/recent-runs.js:67` → `recentRuns(..., RECENT_RUNS)`, `.slice(-limit)` at `:50`). So "every input it reads is already on the recommendation input" isn't true for the attempt check. From the same single read, return the unsliced list for the route and the 5-run slice for the selector. Keep the selector's prompt byte-identical; the stage-router fixtures will show whether it is. Also, the history read is 20 *dispatch rows* (`:65`), counted before autopilot, custom, wake and abort rows are filtered out. The residual-risk line should say 20 rows, not 20 stage runs.
3. **"A run after the comment" should go by dispatch time.** For a finished run, `at` is the time it ended (`lib/recent-runs.js:42`). If a person comments while a Survey is still running, that Survey finishes afterwards, and the comment would read as already acted on. The route would then move past it, which is the override the plan says must never happen. Count a run as "after" the comment only if it was *dispatched* after it (rows carry `dispatchedAt`). Witness: a comment posted mid-run, followed by that run ending, still holds the route.
